topic: Irrealis protasis and the open reading
claim: Of [49] If we weren’t home by ten o’clock the landlady would lock us out, CGEL says that “an irrealis protasis such as if I weren’t home by ten o’clock permits only the remote reading.”
evidence_summary: Ch. 3, p. 87 [33iii] is %If he were surprised, he didn’t show it [past time]: “Example [iii] is a conditional, but of the open type, not the remote”. The same page restricts the use to some speakers (“For some speakers, irrealis were is not restricted to the modal remoteness constructions”) and says that was is “for most speakers probably the only possibility”.
finding: Medium confidence. For speakers who accept [33iii], an irrealis protasis allows the open past-time reading that p. 754 excludes. The defence that p. 754 describes the majority grammar is true, but the unhedged only needs a hedge such as Ch. 3’s for most speakers.
proposed_wording: for most speakers an irrealis protasis such as if I weren’t home by ten o’clock permits only the remote reading (cf. Ch. 3, §1.7)
inference: Does an irrealis protasis exclude the open reading?

evidence.passage: §14.2.2, p. 754. “an irrealis protasis such as if I weren’t home by ten o’clock permits only the remote reading”
evidence.example: Ch. 3, p. 87 [33iii] %If he were surprised, he didn’t show it. The % was confirmed on the page image.
evidence.establishes: The book itself records an open conditional with an irrealis protasis, for some speakers.
